focus: contracted 'd = had · 'd vs would disambiguation · 'had been' /ədbɪn/ · weak 'by the time' / 'before' · past-perfect backgrounding stress
focus_ar: الاختصار 'd = had، والتمييز بينه وبين would، و'had been' الخفيفة، وربط 'by the time' و'before'، ونبر الخلفية في الماضي التام
arabic_challenge: English contracts 'had' to a single /d/ — 'I'd finished' — which sounds exactly like 'I'd' from 'would'. Only the following verb form tells them apart (I'd finished vs I'd finish). Arabic has no such contraction, so learners either expand it unnaturally or lose the past perfect entirely.

isolation.instructions: 'had' contracts to just /d/ on the pronoun: 'I'd finished', 'she'd left', 'they'd gone'. It is a tiny sound, but it changes the whole time frame. Attach it tightly and stress the participle.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'had' تُختصر إلى /d/ فقط: 'I'd finished'. صوت صغير لكنه يغيّر الزمن كله. الصقها وانبر التصريف الثالث.

sentence_practice: By the time I arrived, she'd left.
They'd already eaten when we got there.
I'd never seen anything like it.
daily_drills.record_this: By the time I arrived at the station, she'd already left. They'd finished eating when we finally got there. I'd never seen anything quite like it before that day.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'she'd left'. Can you hear a small /d/ on 'she', with the stress on 'LEFT'?

isolation.instructions: Same /d/, two meanings. The VERB FORM after it decides: 'I'd finished' (participle → had) vs 'I'd finish' (bare verb → would). Listen for the ending, not the contraction.
isolation.instructions_ar: نفس /d/ ومعنيان. شكل الفعل بعده يحدّد: 'I'd finished' (had) مقابل 'I'd finish' (would).

sentence_practice: I'd finish it if I had time.
She'd gone by then; she'd go again tomorrow.
daily_drills.record_this: I'd finished the work before he even called me. I'd finish it tonight if I had a bit more time. She'd already gone by then, though she'd go again tomorrow if we asked her.
daily_drills.self_check: Say both 'I'd finished' and 'I'd finish'. Is the difference in the verb ending, with the /d/ identical?

isolation.instructions: The past perfect continuous stacks three weak sounds: /aɪd bɪn/ + -ing. 'I'd been waiting'. All three compress, and the -ing verb plus the duration take the stress.
isolation.instructions_ar: الماضي التام المستمر يجمع ثلاثة أصوات خفيفة: /aɪd bɪn/ + -ing. الفعل والمدة هما المنبوران.

sentence_practice: I'd been waiting for an hour when she finally arrived.
He was tired because he'd been working all night.
They'd been living there for years before they moved.
daily_drills.record_this: I'd been waiting for over an hour when she finally arrived. He looked exhausted because he'd been working all night. They'd been living in that flat for years before they moved out.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I'd been waiting'. Do /d/ and /bɪn/ both stay weak, with stress on 'WAITing'?

isolation.instructions: Time-ordering phrases are weak and run together: 'baɪðətaɪm', 'bɪfɔː', 'ɑːftə'. Say the phrase quickly, then take a small pause before the main clause: 'By the time I arrived, // she'd left.'
isolation.instructions_ar: عبارات ترتيب الزمن خفيفة ومتصلة: 'baɪðətaɪm'. قلها بسرعة ثم وقفة صغيرة قبل الجملة الرئيسية.

pair: by the time I arrived ❌ (no pause)

word_practice: as soon as we got there
sentence_practice: By the time we arrived, the film had started.
Before I met her, I'd never been abroad.
After they'd eaten, they went for a walk.
daily_drills.record_this: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film had already started. Before I met her, I'd never really been abroad on my own. After they'd eaten dinner, they went for a long walk by the river.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'By the time we arrived, the film had started'. Is the time phrase quick and weak, with a small pause at the comma?

target_sounds: backgrounding stress (past perfect as the earlier layer)

isolation.instructions: The past perfect is BACKGROUND — the earlier layer of the story. Say it slightly lower and faster, then lift your voice for the main past-simple event: 'She'd already left (background) when I ARRIVED (main).'
isolation.instructions_ar: الماضي التام خلفية — الطبقة الأقدم في القصة. قلها أخفض وأسرع، وارفع صوتك للحدث الرئيسي.
practice: she'd already left (lower) → when I ARRIVED (lift)

pair: I'd eaten, so I wasn't hungry
I ate, so I wasn't hungry

sentence_practice: She'd already left when I arrived.
The train had gone by the time we reached the platform.
I wasn't hungry because I'd eaten earlier.
daily_drills.record_this: She'd already left when I finally arrived at the office. The train had gone by the time we reached the platform, so we waited for the next one. I wasn't hungry at all because I'd eaten a big lunch earlier.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'She'd already left when I arrived'. Is the past-perfect part lower and faster, with your voice lifting on 'arrived'?

challenge_sentences: By the time I arrived, she'd already left.
I'd been waiting an hour when he finally called.
I'd finish it tonight if I had time.
Before I met her, I'd never been abroad.
daily_drills.record_this: By the time I arrived at the restaurant, she'd already left. I'd been waiting nearly an hour when he finally called to apologise. I'd finish the whole thing tonight if I had a little more time. Before I met her, I'd never really been abroad alone.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: a tiny /d/ for 'had', weak 'been' in 'd been, and the past perfect kept lower as background.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself telling a story about a trip that went wrong, using the past perfect for everything that happened earlier. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تحكي قصة رحلة فشلت، مستخدمًا الماضي التام لكل ما حدث قبلها، وبعدين اسمع وراجع.
test_yourself.passage: Last summer we planned a short trip, and almost everything went wrong. By the time we reached the airport, the check-in desk had closed. I'd booked the tickets weeks earlier, but I'd written down the wrong departure time. My brother was furious because he'd woken up at four in the morning for nothing. We'd been planning that holiday for months, and we'd already paid for the hotel. When we finally got a later flight, we discovered our luggage hadn't arrived with us. It had been sitting in another airport for two days. By the time it reached us, the trip had almost finished. Looking back, I'd never made such a silly mistake before, and I haven't made it since.

sounds_to_check.contracted 'd = had: I'd booked, I'd written, he'd woken, we'd already paid, I'd never made
sounds_to_check.'d been' /dbɪn/: we'd been planning, it had been sitting
sounds_to_check.full 'had' where needed: the desk had closed, our luggage hadn't arrived, it had been sitting
sounds_to_check.weak time phrases + pause: By the time we reached the airport, // By the time it reached us, //
sounds_to_check.backgrounding: past perfect lower and faster, past simple lifted (went wrong, discovered, got)

scoring_guide.90_100: Clear tiny /d/, weak 'been', and a real two-layer story. Ready for week 3.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasional expanded 'had' or a flat background layer.
scoring_guide.50_69: Past perfect lost or over-pronounced, so the time order is unclear. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, contracting 'had' to /d/ and keeping the earlier layer lower.

for_arabic_speakers: 'had' becomes a single /d/ on the pronoun — small sound, big change in time frame.
'd = had' and ''d = would' sound identical; only the verb form after it tells them apart.
In ''d been' both the /d/ and /bɪn/ stay weak; stress the -ing verb and the duration.
Keep the past perfect lower and faster — it is background. Lift your voice for the main past-simple event.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
